channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is now exploited, days after two others were patched
item.category: Top Story
item.description: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure. The new flaw, CVE-2026-88779 (CVSS v4 8.7), is a memory overflow affecting only SAML-configured appliances; watchTowr reproduced it as a crash bug, and one researcher’s claim of code execution is disputed. CISA added it to KEV on 4 October, and the federal deadline passed on 7 October. The earlier pair, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and configuration theft, and patching does not evict an intruder, so appliances fixed last week need a second upgrade. NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, making an unhunted appliance a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174; CISA KEV catalog; Dutch NCSC; Tenable, watchTowr, LevelBlue, Arctic Wolf and Mandiant/GTIG research; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - CVE-2026-88779 fixed 3–4 Oct and added to KEV 4 Oct 2026 (deadline 7 Oct, now passed); watchTowr denial-of-service finding and CISA/Australian warnings 5 Oct 2026 (SecurityWeek and The Record, 5 Oct); first two flaws confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026, mass exploitation after a 28 Sep proof-of-concept write-up; post-exploitation analysis 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement (18 Sep 2026), reported by Axios Denver and Industrial Cyber (22 Sep) - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [Medium] Southern Company says about 400,000 Georgia Power and Alabama Power customer accounts were accessed through the online portal
item.category: Incident — unauthorized access to customer-portal accounts at Southern Company utilities; customer data exposed; no operational impact reported; access method undisclosed
item.description: Southern Company disclosed on 7 October that an unauthorized party got into customer accounts on the online portals of its Georgia Power and Alabama Power subsidiaries, with Mississippi Power also named. The company puts the total at roughly 400,000 accounts, about 300,000 at Georgia Power and 100,000 at Alabama Power. Exposed data includes names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, the last four digits of Social Security numbers and basic account details; bank account, payment card and driver’s licence numbers were not accessed. The utility says it acted to stop the activity once detected, has engaged law enforcement and is offering a year of credit monitoring. Neither the timing of the intrusion nor how the attacker got in has been disclosed, and no operational or grid impact was reported. For OT defenders it is an IT-side customer-data event, but it underlines how customer-facing portals at large utilities draw determined attackers. - Southern Company statement, reported by SecurityWeek - Disclosed 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Vicksburg, Mississippi shuts down city systems after a ransomware attack that disrupted utility payments
item.category: Incident — ransomware at a Mississippi city government; utility payment systems and city computers disrupted; emergency services reported unaffected; actor unidentified; no OT impact reported
item.description: Vicksburg, Mississippi Mayor Willis Thompson said in a 1 October statement, reported by The Record the next day, that the city had taken systems offline after a ransomware incident, calling the shutdown temporary. Utility bill payment systems were disrupted while emergency services were not, and the mayor said no one’s services would be shut off and no late-payment penalties issued during the investigation. Whether personal data was compromised is still under investigation. The FBI, DHS, state officials and private responders are assisting; no group has claimed the attack, and the city declined to discuss any ransom demand. Nothing reported points to water, wastewater or power control systems being affected. For small municipal utilities it is another reminder that billing and administrative IT often fails first and can force manual operations. - Vicksburg mayor’s statement, reported by The Record - Mayor’s statement 1 Oct 2026; reported 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Hackers reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system, Bloomberg reports; the FBI says there was no disruption
item.category: Incident — Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed US officials, that hackers temporarily reached the propulsion system of the US-bound tanker VL Prosperity; FBI on record: no operational disruption, instability or crew danger; actor, duration and extent of control unknown; a second tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials who asked not to be named, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had temporarily accessed the propulsion system of the very large crude carrier VL Prosperity as it approached the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and Bloomberg says it is unclear how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control. No one has been publicly blamed. VL Prosperity was boarded in the Atlantic on 21 August after it lost communications, and a second, unnamed tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico days later. Earlier engine-room manipulation claims from Iranian media remain unverified. - Bloomberg (citing unnamed US officials), via Supply Chain Brain and gCaptain; FBI statement; boarding details per the US Coast Guard, Dragos and Reuters - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-system access reported 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
item.category: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 7 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and SOCRadar’s latest count is 86,644 compromised devices. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary. - FBI and US Secret Service warning, reported by The Hacker News, BleepingComputer and The Record; CISA mitigation guidance (June 2026) - Ongoing — re-warned 7 Oct 2026 (BleepingComputer and The Hacker News, 7 Oct); campaign first documented June 2026

item.title: [Medium] Boston Scientific’s August incident shows how IT-side damage can disrupt plants without touching controls
item.category: Incident — Boston Scientific cyber incident that entered through an external-facing network device; the company’s 22 Sep update, citing CrowdStrike, found no compromise of SCADA or plant-maintenance systems; systems fully restored by 9 Sep
item.description: Boston Scientific said in a 22 September update, citing CrowdStrike’s final findings, that an attacker got in through an external-facing network device on 25 August and reached a limited portion of its on-premises IT environment. The company found no evidence of compromise in its SCADA, manufacturing-maintenance, product-development or medical-device-maintenance systems, and no evidence that data was accessed or taken. It disclosed the incident in an SEC filing on 26 August and had fully restored systems by 9 September. An Industrial Cyber expert analysis on 30 September, which reports manufacturing disruption at the company’s Cork, Ireland site, uses the case to make the dependency point for plant defenders: when ERP, ordering and logistics systems go down, production suffers even if the control network is clean. - Boston Scientific incident updates (26 Aug–22 Sep 2026), citing CrowdStrike; Industrial Cyber expert analysis (30 Sep 2026) - Attack 25 Aug 2026; disclosed 26 Aug; systems restored by 9 Sep; final findings 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Warlock ransomware attackers keep breaking in through on-premises SharePoint, now including a water utility
item.category: Incident — Symantec reports the China-nexus actor it calls Longlegs (Storm-2603) deploying Warlock ransomware through on-premises SharePoint flaws, with a water utility and a telecom provider among at least four recent victims; no OT impact described
item.description: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team reported on 1 October that over the past two months the group it calls Longlegs (also tracked as Storm-2603), which deploys Warlock ransomware, attacked at least four organizations in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries across Europe, Africa and Latin America: a water utility, a telecom provider, a regional government body and a university. Symantec says Longlegs typically gets in by exploiting on-premises SharePoint Server; the only CVEs it names are the 2025 “ToolShell” flaws, plus related SharePoint bugs. The tooling includes web shells, stolen ASP.NET machine keys, DLL sideloading, a Visual Studio Code tunnel and a vulnerable K7 driver used to switch off security software. Symantec describes Longlegs as a China-nexus actor; that is its own assessment. No victims are named, and Symantec describes no operational-technology impact at the water utility. - Symantec Threat Hunter Team report; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer and Industrial Cyber - Report published 1 Oct 2026; activity over roughly the previous two months

item.title: [Critical] Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
item.category: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 18 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass and a persistent command-injection flaw; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE disclosed 18 vulnerabilities in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters on 16 September in advisory VDE-2026-014. The worst, CVE-2026-27546, is an authentication bypass scored CVSS 9.8; a companion flaw, CVE-2026-27565, lets an attacker inject operating-system commands through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. Nozomi Networks’ 29 September write-up counts 19 flaws in the ICE2 model and says two HTTPS requests are enough to take root. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover. - CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014 - Published 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi technical write-up 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Ransomware volume hit a 2026 high in August, and industrial organizations took roughly a third of it
item.category: Threat intel — NCC Group’s August 2026 ransomware review counts 1,073 attacks, up 12% on July, with the industrial sector the target in about 31%; Qilin leads; no CVE
item.description: NCC Group’s review of August 2026, reported by Industrial Cyber on 28 September, recorded 1,073 ransomware attacks, a 12% rise on July. Industrial organizations were the target in 329 of them (31%), and North America took 44% of all victims. Qilin was the most active operator with 164 incidents (15%), overtaking The Gentlemen. The report also flags Aurora, a ransomware-as-a-service group active since late April that goes after manufacturing and transport using VPN exploitation, credential harvesting and hypervisor encryption — the same remote-access edge covered elsewhere in this edition. These are victim-leak-site counts, so they measure claimed attacks rather than confirmed operational shutdowns. - NCC Group monthly threat report, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 28 Sep 2026; covers August 2026 activity

item.title: [Medium] CISA’s 1 October ICS batch: EV-charging and ABB engineering-software flaws with no fixed version yet
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS batch of 1 Oct 2026 (ICSA-26-274-01 to -06) covering Armatura One access control, Monta EV charging, ABB PCM600, Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo and Meari IoT Cloud; several products have no fixed version; no known exploitation
item.description: CISA released six ICS advisories on 1 October. Armatura One physical-access-control software before 4.7.2 (USA builds before 4.6.1) embeds the ActiveMQ deserialization flaw CVE-2023-46604 (CVSS 9.8), a bug ransomware crews have used against other ActiveMQ deployments, though no Armatura-specific exploitation is reported, plus hard-coded keys and credentials. The Monta EV-charging platform has a missing-authentication WebSocket flaw, CVE-2026-95102 (CVSS v3.1 9.4), that allows charging-station impersonation; there is no fixed version, only Monta’s configuration guidance and vendor-side rate limiting. ABB PCM600 2.14 and earlier has privilege-escalation and path-traversal flaws with a workaround but no fixed version. Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo controllers have two lower-severity flaws fixed in new firmware, and Meari IoT Cloud has authorization flaws with no fix planned. CISA reports no known exploitation of any of them. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-274-01 to -06; ABB advisories 2NGA003170 / 2NGA003179 - Released 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CVSS 10.0 flaws in Toptech’s terminal-management software lead CISA’s 29 September ICS batch
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS batch of 29 Sep 2026 (ICSA-26-272-01 to -07), led by Toptech TMS7/TopHAT 7.6.3 (CVE-2026-71379, CVSS 10.0); also Lantronix G520 cellular gateways, VIVOTEK cameras (CVSS 10.0, public proof-of-concept) and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-84411; no known exploitation
item.description: CISA released seven ICS advisories on 29 September. The most serious for operators is ICSA-26-272-02: ten flaws in Toptech Systems’ TMS7 and TopHAT 7.6.3, software used to run fuel and bulk-liquid terminals (our description; CISA lists the energy, chemical and transportation sectors). The worst, CVE-2026-71379, exposes files to outside parties and scores CVSS 10.0; others include an unrestricted file upload (9.1) and five SQL injections (9.0), which CISA says could let an attacker reach critical data or run code. Release 7.8 fixes them, and Toptech notified customers in July. The batch also covers Lantronix G520 cellular gateways (fixed in 2.6.0.7R6; CISA lists water, energy and transportation), a VIVOTEK camera command-injection flaw (CVSS 10.0) with public proof-of-concept code, and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-84411 (CVSS 9.8, fixed in 7.24), which is not in KEV. Baicells, Anjvision and Viidure products in the batch have no fix planned. CISA reports no known exploitation of any of them. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-272-01 to -07 - Released 29 Sep 2026; Toptech customer advisory 20 Jul 2026

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway/Spark VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers/SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September alongside flaws in Arista VeloCloud and F5 BIG-IP APM; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites. - Check Point security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security - Exploitation confirmed by 22 Sep 2026; KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [High] F5 BIG-IP APM zero-day: unauthenticated code execution on OAuth servers, exploited and past its federal deadline
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-94127, F5 BIG-IP APM configured as an OAuth authorization server; heap overflow, unauthenticated remote code execution (CVSS 9.8 v3.1); exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on 22 September: a heap-based buffer overflow in BIG-IP Access Policy Manager that gives an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution when APM is set up as an OAuth authorization server. Systems using APM only as a client or resource server are not affected. The flaw is being exploited, CISA added it to KEV the same day, and the 25 September federal deadline has passed. BIG-IP appliances commonly front remote-access and vendor portals into industrial networks, so an exposed one is a path toward OT even though it runs no control loop. - F5 security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by The Hacker News - F5 advisory and KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [High] Cisco warns of a fifth SD-WAN zero-day this year: an authentication bypass in SD-WAN Manager is being exploited
item.category: Advisory — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504, Cisco CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; fixed releases available; added to CISA KEV 30 Sep 2026 with a 3 Oct federal deadline, now passed; advisory revised 2 Oct; exploiting actor not named
item.description: Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504, a flaw in how Catalyst SD-WAN Manager handles URI encoding, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass an authentication rule protecting an API endpoint and gain administrator-level access. Cisco rates it CVSS 9.8, says it became aware of active exploitation in September without naming an actor, and lists no workarounds. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 3 October federal deadline, now passed, and Cisco revised its advisory on 2 October. Fixed releases exist for each supported train; releases older than 20.9 must migrate. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth SD-WAN zero-day exploited in 2026. In our assessment (editorial, not from the source), SD-WAN managers often control the WAN links that tie remote substations, plants and pipeline sites back to headquarters, so administrator takeover is a path toward those sites. - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer - Disclosed and added to KEV 30 Sep 2026; advisory revised 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet confirms an exploited FortiMail zero-day, and its updated advisory now lists fixed releases
item.category: Advisory — Fortinet FortiMail path-traversal / NULL-byte zero-day (CVE-2026-104286, Fortinet CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 1 Oct 2026 (deadline 4 Oct); Fortinet’s 5 Oct update lists fixed releases
item.description: Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-175 describes a path-traversal and NULL-byte handling flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on a FortiMail appliance through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests. Fortinet scores it CVSS 9.8 and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV on 1 October with a three-day federal deadline. Affected branches are 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 8.0. When the advisory first appeared the fixes were only planned, but Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2, and tells 7.2 users to move to the 7.4 branch or later. In our assessment (editorial), FortiMail is an email gateway rather than an OT product, but it sits in the corporate trust zone that many plant networks inherit accounts and mail relays from, so a compromised gateway is a stepping stone worth closing off. - Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-175; CISA KEV catalog; reported by SecurityWeek - Disclosed and added to KEV 1 Oct 2026; fixed releases listed in Fortinet’s 5 Oct 2026 update

item.title: [Critical] A critical bug in the lwIP network stack embedded in countless controllers and gateways lets an attacker run code remotely
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01: out-of-bounds write in the lwIP embedded TCP/IP stack’s MQTT client, CVE-2026-87121, CVSS 9.8; public proof-of-concept reported; not in CISA KEV
item.description: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-265-01 on 22 September for CVE-2026-87121 (CVSS 9.8), an out-of-bounds write in the MQTT client component of lwIP, a widely embedded open-source TCP/IP stack. An unauthenticated network attacker could gain code execution on a device that uses the vulnerable MQTT client. Because lwIP ships inside many vendors’ firmware, exposure depends on whether a given product enables the MQTT client and which vendor has issued a rebuilt image. A public proof-of-concept has been reported, but the flaw is not in CISA’s exploited-vulnerabilities catalog and no in-the-wild use is confirmed. Asset owners will mostly be waiting on their device vendors. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01; corroborated by CVE record aggregators - Advisory published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] SonicWall ships hotfixes for a maximum-severity flaw in SMA1000 remote-access gateways
item.category: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, a server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated, remote, low complexity; no exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV
item.description: SonicWall released hotfixes on 6 October for CVE-2026-102255, a server-side request forgery in the Appliance WorkPlace interface of SMA1000 gateways, which it rates as maximum severity. BleepingComputer reports the flaw can be reached remotely without authentication and with low complexity. It affects the SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; the SMA100 series and SSL-VPN on SonicWall firewalls are not affected. SonicWall says it has no evidence of exploitation, and Shadowserver counts more than 400 internet-exposed SMA1000 appliances, some possibly already patched. The report gives no CVSS number or fixed version, so check the vendor advisory. Remote-access gateways like this are a common route for vendors and integrators into plant networks. - SonicWall advisory, reported by BleepingComputer; Shadowserver exposure data - Hotfixes released 6 Oct 2026; reported 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Industry coalition asks CISA for a binding directive on OT security inside federal agencies
item.category: Policy — OT Cybersecurity Coalition urges CISA to issue a binding operational directive on OT security at federal agencies; a proposal only, no CISA commitment; no CVE
item.description: The OT Cybersecurity Coalition is urging CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive focused solely on operational technology at federal civilian agencies, CyberScoop reported on 6 October. The coalition wants each agency to name an accountable OT cybersecurity officer, meet minimum practices drawn from existing federal guidance and CISA’s 2022 Cybersecurity Performance Goals, and consider whether NSA’s OT guidance should apply to civilian agencies. It points to a 30 September GAO report finding that only 7 of 22 civilian agencies fully met OMB’s requirements for networked IoT and OT devices, and to this summer’s water-utility attacks. CISA did not respond to CyberScoop and has announced no directive. In our assessment, a directive would bind only federal agencies but would signal what CISA expects of OT programs generally. - OT Cybersecurity Coalition paper, reported by CyberScoop; GAO-26-108937 - Reported 6 Oct 2026; GAO report 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] DOE opens $100 million cybersecurity assistance program for rural, municipal and small electric utilities
item.category: Policy — DOE announces a $100 million technical-assistance initiative for rural, municipal and small electric utilities; no CVE
item.description: The Department of Energy, through its Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) and administrator ConnectWerx, has launched the Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity advanced technical assistance partnership. Not-for-profit intermediaries that partner with at least six qualifying utilities can apply to deliver assessments, workforce training, exercises, technology deployment and threat-information sharing to electric cooperatives, municipal utilities and small investor-owned utilities. DOE’s announcement gives no application deadline. For small operators with thin security budgets, it is a possible route to outside OT assessment help. - DOE CESER announcement; reported by Industrial Cyber - Announced 1 Oct 2026; reported 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] GAO: overlapping federal incident-reporting rules burden critical infrastructure operators
item.category: Policy — GAO report GAO-26-109197 on duplicative and conflicting federal cyber-incident reporting rules, based on an industry panel; no formal recommendations; no CVE
item.description: A Government Accountability Office report published on 28 September (GAO-26-109197) drew on a July panel of six industry representatives from energy, financial services and healthcare. They described duplicative and conflicting federal and sector-specific cyber-incident reporting rules, saying it can be hard to meet every reporting requirement while also remediating an attack. Participants proposed consistent timeframes, thresholds and definitions, a lead agency such as CISA to coordinate reporting, and more government-industry collaboration; half said harmonization progress has been limited. GAO made no formal recommendations. For OT operators, the practical effect is that one incident can trigger several reporting clocks at once. - US Government Accountability Office (GAO-26-109197); reported by Cybersecurity Dive and Industrial Cyber - Published 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
item.category: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion
item.description: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk on 24 September, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers referenced in the guidance include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised. - FBI and CISA joint fact sheet; reported by Industrial Cyber - Released 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — comments are open until 30 November
item.category: Guidance — NIST releases initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security”; expanded sector scope, restructured around CSF 2.0; comment period through 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime vessels; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026, and it lands the same week as the FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above). - NIST Computer Security Resource Center; reported by SecurityWeek and Industrial Cyber - Draft published 21 Sep 2026; comments due 30 Nov 2026
